niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want structured Jungian shadow work, a broader spiritual framework, or a regular meditation practice. These are good starting points from the options I found:

### Shadow work
- **[Encounters with the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)** — A compact introduction to Jungian shadow concepts, with videos, audio, and a companion guide. A good pick if you want to explore the ideas before committing to a longer course.
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A broader course featuring multiple teachers and practical exercises. Consider this if you want varied perspectives and tools to try in daily life.
- **[Diving into the Shadow — Michael Lennox](https://michaellennox.com/classes/shadow/)** — A four-week online course with a defined time frame; the listing I found gives a price of $99, though you should check the site for current availability and cost.
- **[Befriending the Shadow: A Jungian Experiential Inquiry](https://jungian.directory/courses/befriending-the-shadow-a-jungian-experiential-inquiry/)** — A four-week experiential course focused on personal and collective shadow through depth psychology.

### Spiritual practice and meditation
- **[The Three Turnings of the Wheel — Naropa University](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — A series of six-week online courses rooted in Buddhist study, contemplation, meditation, and compassion practice.
- **[Mindfulness and Well-being: Peace In, Peace Out — Rice University Online](https://online.rice.edu/courses/mindfulness-and-well-being-peace-in-peace-out)** — Self-paced mindfulness training that includes material on spiritual development.
- **[Mindfulness Meditation: The Fundamentals — Jack Kornfield](https://jackkornfield.com/all-courses/)** — A practical introduction to mindfulness and compassion meditations, including work with breath, body, feelings, and thoughts.
- **[Closer Than Breath — Shalem](https://shalem.org/programs/offerings-by-shalem-graduates/)** — A six-week, self-paced course in Centering Prayer, especially suited to a contemplative Christian or interfaith approach.

**Quick picks:** For a short Jungian introduction, try *Encounters with the Shadow*; for practical exercises and multiple viewpoints, *Engage the Shadow*; for a sustained meditation path, consider Naropa or Jack Kornfield.

A note on safety: shadow work can bring up painful memories or intense emotions. Choose a course that encourages pacing and grounding, and treat it as personal development—not a substitute for therapy. If you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress, consider working with a qualified mental-health professional alongside any course. Check each provider’s site for current dates, prices, instructor details, and whether the course is self-paced or live.
